subject: MSA & Order Form: maintenance window freeze proposal and credit cap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@sunnivahealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@sunnivahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA & Order Form: maintenance window freeze proposal and credit cap

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Sunniva's launch timeline is tight, and we want to lock down a few items in the MSA + Order Form to avoid last-minute schedule risk. Attached are the redlines we discussed (redlines_MSA_v3.pdf) and the SLA matrix for the Order Form (orderform_sla_matrix.xlsx).

Key asks from our side:
- Maintenance window freeze during your first 90 days of production (no rolling maintenance that impacts your primary region).
- Service credit cap of 5% of monthly recurring charges per month, with a 12-month aggregate cap at 15% — we think this balances accountability and predictable exposure.
- P1 response time: 1 hour initial response, 4 hour mitigation plan.
- Change-control for scheduled maintenance: 60 days notice for any blackout window changes after signing.

Sam — if Sunniva can accept the freeze for the first 90 days and the credit cap above, we can prioritize a signed Order Form and reserve dedicated capacity for your go-live week.

Lauren / Kimberly — looping you in for legal and procurement sign-off on the MSA language. Please advise if the 90-day freeze or the credit cap are non-starters; also flag any escalation path language we need to add.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlines_MSA_v3.pdf (redlined MSA), orderform_sla_matrix.xlsx (proposed SLAs)
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@sunnivahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@sunnivahealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form: maintenance window freeze proposal and credit cap

Marissa —

Appreciate the summary and the files. Sunniva legal has reviewed and provided some counterpoints (see attached redlines_MSA_v3.pdf) — main items from our side:
1) We cannot accept a hard freeze on maintenance beyond 30 days for production. We can agree to a 30-day operational lock during the initial go-live and a mutually agreed blackout week for launch activities.
2) Service credit cap — procurement is OK with a cap but requests a floor of 3% and an absolute ceiling of 10% depending on uptime tiers.
3) We need clarification on how you measure downtime (per-region vs global) and require inclusion of monitoring evidence (uptime dashboards) as part of credit calculations.
4) For P1 response, we can agree on 1 hour initial acknowledgement, but mitigation timing should be an SLA-to-target (e.g., mitigation started within 4 hours) with exceptions for force majeure and customer-induced issues.

We also suggested a short change-control clause that requires a 30-day notice plus a 5-business-day operational sync before any maintenance affecting production.

We can jump on Tuesday to reconcile. In principle Sunniva wants predictable availability for their care portal launch, but they also need Redwood to retain the ability to schedule urgent security fixes.

Thanks,
Sam Turner
Head of Cloud Ops | Sunniva Health
sam.turner@sunnivahealth.com

Attachments: sunniva_redlines_MSA_comments.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@sunnivahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form: maintenance window freeze proposal and credit cap

Thanks Sam — helpful notes.

To summarize Sunniva's counterproposal and our suggested compromise so legal can craft the language:
- Production maintenance freeze: Redwood accepts a 30-day operational lock around go-live (we'll label it "Initial Launch Lock"). After that, maintenance affecting the primary region will require 30 days' notice plus a 5-business-day operational sync. Redwood will maintain the right to schedule emergency security patches with an obligation to notify and minimize impact.
- Service credits: propose a tiered model in the Order Form: 99.9% uptime => 2% credit, 99.5-99.9% => 5% credit, <99.5% => 10% credit capped at 10% monthly (we are pushing to 5% earlier, but can accept 10% cap if tiers are explicit).
- Measurement: credits calculated on per-region availability; evidence required is Redwood's public uptime dashboard + internal incident reports. Credits are applied to the monthly invoice.
- P1 response: 1 hour to acknowledge, mitigation plan within 4 hours; rolling updates every 2 hours until resolution or handoff to post-incident review.

Kimberly / Lauren — can you draft MSA and Order Form language reflecting the Initial Launch Lock (30 days), the emergency patch carveout, and the tiered credit schedule above? If legal prefers different caps, flag the commercial impact (we may need to reserve capacity or change pricing).

Sam / Priya — if you agree with the compromise above, we'll prepare a final Order Form and DocuSign packet for signature.

Best,

Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA & Order Form: maintenance window freeze proposal and credit cap

Marissa / Lauren —

Thanks for the write-up — I drafted proposed contract language and inserted it into redlines_MSA_v3.pdf (see attachment). High-level notes:
- "Initial Launch Lock": we will state 30 calendar days of no planned maintenance that impacts production region(s) starting at customer go-live. Exceptions: emergency security patches (defined as CVSS 7.0+) and customer-requested maintenance.
- Credit schedule: adopted tiered credits with an absolute monthly cap of 10% (legal is not comfortable with a unilateral 5% cap since that may undercompensate customers for sustained outages). We inserted a 12-month aggregation clause that prevents credits exceeding 25% of total paid during first 12 months (commercial compromise).
- Measurement & evidence: credits are calculated per-region and require Redwood incident report + the uptime dashboard export. We excluded third-party infra failures where Redwood had no control.
- Change control: 30-day notice for schedule changes; for post-signing changes that impact availability commitments, we'll require mutual written agreement.

Action items:
- Marissa: confirm commercial acceptance of the 10% monthly cap with the 12-month aggregate cap and we will push to legal for final wording.
- Lauren: prepare procurement checklist and routing for sign-off (billing, security attestation).
- Sam / Priya: if Sunniva can accept the 30-day Initial Launch Lock + emergency patch carveout and the credit aggregation clause, Kimberly will finalize the language and we can circulate a DocuSign.

I'll attach the updated PDF in the next email (redlines_MSA_v4.pdf).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
